issue.issue_text: Whether the continuation of the criminal proceedings against the appellants would be justified, when the matter has been compromised between the borrower and Bank.

facts: A criminal case was initiated against the appellants (borrowers) in a financial matter involving a bank.
Subsequently, the appellants and the bank reached a compromise through a One-Time Settlement (OTS).
The appellants paid the agreed settlement amount, and the bank closed the loan account, confirming the settlement.
Despite this resolution, the criminal proceedings continued, and the High Court declined to quash them under Section 482 of the CrPC.
law: The Supreme Court considered the High Court's inherent power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) to quash criminal proceedings.

The Court cited the principle that in cases arising from commercial, financial, or other similar transactions where the wrong is primarily private and the parties have resolved their entire dispute, the court should exercise its power to end the criminal proceedings.
application: The Court determined that the core dispute between the borrower and the bank had been fully settled.
It reasoned that once the financial matter is compromised, the possibility of a conviction in the related criminal case becomes "remote and bleak."
The Court found that continuing the criminal proceedings after the settlement would cause "great oppression and prejudice" to the appellants and would not be justifiable.
The Court also referenced a separate judgment it had delivered on the same day in a case with similar facts, where it had reached the same conclusion.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the continuation of the criminal proceedings was not justified because the underlying financial dispute between the borrower and the bank had been fully compromised. Therefore, the Court quashed the criminal proceedings against the appellants.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the continuation of the criminal proceedings against the appellants would be justified, when the matter has been compromised between the borrower and Bank.
appellant_arguments: The appellants had no active role to play in the alleged offences and were implicated only because they are related to Accused No. 2.
In light of the compromise between the borrower and the Bank, the criminal proceedings should be quashed, a position supported by previous judgments of the Supreme Court.
